name: Vasiswarar Temple, Thiruppasur
deity: Shiva as Vasiswarar (Vaseeswarar), the lingam found in the bamboo forest, with the Goddess Pasupathinayaki and Thangadhali
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu, sung in the Tevaram by Appar and Sambandar (7th century)
dynasty: Chola, with traditions of Karikala Chola
summary: Just west of Tiruvallur, in what was once a forest of bamboo, Shiva is worshipped as Vasiswarar — the lingam uncovered where a cow let her milk flow, still bearing the mark of the blade that struck it.

sections.history: Thiruppasur — also written Thiruppachur — is a village about five kilometres from Tiruvallur on the road to Tiruttani, and its name recalls the bamboo, pasu, that once grew thick here. Its temple to Shiva as Vasiswarar is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams, a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Thondai Nadu sung in the Tevaram by both Appar and Sambandar. Tradition credits the building of the temple to Karikala Chola, the great early king of the Chola line, after the lingam was discovered in the forest, and inscriptions of the Chola period remain on its walls.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian shrine of the Tiruvallur plain, with the sanctum of Vasiswarar and the shrines of the Goddess within its enclosure. The lingam is honoured for the scar it bears, the mark said to have been left at the time of its finding. Beside the Lord stands the shrine of Thangadhali, understood as the divine couple in their wedding form, together with the Goddess Pasupathinayaki — two aspects of the Mother in a single temple.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that in the bamboo forest a cow was seen letting her milk flow, unbidden, over a single spot. When the ground was dug, a lingam was found — and the blade of a vaasi, an axe-like tool, struck it and left a wound. From that tool the Lord takes the name Vasiswarar. Tradition adds that Karikala Chola, threatened by a serpent sent by his enemies, prayed here and was saved by the Lord's grace, and that the Goddess Thangadhali, after worshipping Shiva, joined him to bless all who come.
sections.festivals: Pradosham and Maha Shivaratri are kept with special worship, together with Karthigai Deepam and the temple's annual brahmotsavam. Days sacred to the Goddess are observed at the shrine of Thangadhali; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thiruppasur is a quiet village temple, an easy stop from Tiruvallur, and it rewards the pilgrim who comes for its story: the wounded lingam of the bamboo forest, honoured for more than a thousand years. Many pair a visit here with the Veeraraghava Perumal temple in Tiruvallur town and with the other Tevaram shrines of the district, among them Thiruvalangadu and Koovam.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer areas, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruppasur lies about 5 km from Tiruvallur on the Tiruvallur–Tiruttani road, a short bus or auto ride from the Tiruvallur bus stand. Tiruvallur is a station on the Chennai–Arakkonam suburban line, and Chennai International Airport is the nearest airport.
